properties.name: Exactly one commit on a branch writes the design export, and it should be the last
properties.statement:
A branch may hold as many commits as it likes. EXACTLY ONE of them may write `docs/design/reflow2.json`, and it should be the last one. Export straight onto the committed file rather than exporting elsewhere and copying it in — the lineage link is built from whatever file is already at that path.

ENFORCED, AND THAT IS A MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN A JUDGEMENT. Breaking this ALREADY stops the build: `tools/reflow2_check.py` fails with `FAIL LINEAGE` and CI goes red. It did so twice on 2026-08-11 in one day's work. So `enforced: true` records what the project already does, not a consequence anybody chose today. ⚠️ Anthony has NOT been asked the consequence question for this rule — `cap:governance-proposal` exists to ask it and was not run. If he would rather this were advisory, the flag is wrong and the CI gate is what should change, not the flag.

WHY THIS RULE EXISTS SEPARATELY FROM THE REQUIREMENT IT SHADOWS, which is the whole point of adding it. `req:the-export-is-serialised-rather-than-socially-enforced` (accepted) says the SOFTWARE must detect a severed chain, and it is fully traced: `art:check` satisfies it and `ver:gate-suite` verifies that artifact. That thread is about what reflow2 BUILDS. It says nothing about what a CONTRIBUTOR must do, and the governance layer — `unverified_enforced_rule`, which scans DesignRules — could not see this policy at all, because the policy was expressed only as a requirement on the tool.

⇒ THE DETECTOR WAS REQUIRED AND BUILT; THE BEHAVIOUR WAS A CONVENTION WITH NO GOVERNANCE NODE. Anthony, 2026-08-11: "reflow2's own rules shouldn't be tracked by hand, but by some governance rules." This is that rule, made first-class.

HOW TO FOLLOW IT, recorded because it is not derivable and it cost about ten hand-driven cycles in a single day: restore the committed file first (`git checkout origin/main -- docs/design/reflow2.json`), then `export_graph` ONCE, then commit — folding into the existing commit with `--amend` if the branch already has one. ⚠️ A LINEAGE FAILURE REPORTED LOCALLY IMMEDIATELY AFTER EXPORTING IS EXPECTED AND IS NOT THE DEFECT: the local gate compares against HEAD's committed export while CI compares against the primary branch's, so amend first and re-check. The reverse also holds — a local OK after a rebase is not proof, because the three-way merge driver merges CONTENT correctly and cannot repair LINEAGE, which is a property of the file-to-file chain.

SCOPE, stated because the sibling rule does not state its own and is partly unfollowable without a forge. THIS RULE IS EXPRESSIBLE IN PURE GIT: one commit per branch touches one file. It needs no pull request, no forge and no review model. A PR is merely where CI happens to notice, which is why the rule survives on a bare remote where `rule:nothing-lands-on-main-directly` does not.

WHAT IT DOES NOT SAY: nothing about who may merge, nothing about branch naming, and nothing about review. Those are separate conventions and this rule deliberately does not smuggle them in.
